notes.text: **Mass:** how much _________, in _________________. Stays the same when you travel.   **Weight:** the force of __________, in ______________. Changes when gravity changes.

rows.title: Newton’s Three Laws

notes: *2nd law: Fnet = _____, so a = ___________. Fnet is the _____ of all forces.

notes.text: Same mass: more net force, ______ acceleration. Same force, twice the mass: ______ the acceleration.

notes: *3rd law: for every action, there is an ________ and ___________ reaction.

notes.text: The pair acts on _____ objects, so third-law forces do not _________ on one object’s FBD.

conceptReview.title: Unit 3 / Concept Review
conceptReview.subtitle: Connect the ideas, check common mix-ups, and explain the physics in your own words.

sections.heading: Newton’s laws
paragraphs: Mass (kg) never changes; weight, Fg = mg (N), depends on g. Fnet = 0 means constant velocity; otherwise Fnet = ma.
sections.watchOut: A moving object does not need a net force to keep moving.

sections.heading: Free-body diagrams
paragraphs: One object, one labeled arrow per force. Add with signs; split an angled force into Fx = F cos θ and Fy = F sin θ.
sections.watchOut: Third-law pairs act on two objects, so they never cancel on one FBD.

sections.heading: Forces on an incline
paragraphs: Tilt the axes: Fg,parallel = mg sin θ down the slope, Fg,perp = mg cos θ into the ramp, and FN = mg cos θ.
sections.watchOut: Normal force does not always equal weight. A steeper ramp gives a smaller FN.

sections.heading: Net force and acceleration
paragraphs: a = Fnet / m, in the direction of Fnet. Frictionless ramp: a = g sin θ. Elevator, up positive: FN − mg = ma.
sections.watchOut: The scale reads FN, which changes with acceleration, not with moving up or down.

sections.heading: Friction
paragraphs: Static friction matches the need, up to fs,max = μsFN. Sliding friction, fk ≈ μkFN, is usually smaller.
sections.watchOut: Find FN first. An angled pull or a ramp changes it.

sections.heading: Connected objects
paragraphs: Ideal rope: one tension T, one size of a. Find a from the whole system, then T from one object’s Fnet = ma.
sections.watchOut: Draw a separate FBD for each object.

quickRecall: Write the weight components for a block on a ramp.
Explain why a scale reads more in an elevator accelerating up.
